title: ERA Residence - Day-Night Light Switch as Hero Control

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A wall light switch or short travel slider: one decisive motion flips the room between lit and dark.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: The first control under the wordmark is a short BY DAY / BY NIGHT slider; moving it re-lights the hero photography - blue sky, palms, bougainvillea vs the same white terraces after sunset. It sits at the optical centre as the only touchable thing besides the scroll cue: the day/night flip IS the sales argument (buying a second home = buying light).

design_tokens.borders: Hairline letterspaced-caps wordmark; slider as a short track with a thumb, no heavy chrome
design_tokens.elevation: Flat photography; state change handled by re-lighting imagery, not shadows
design_tokens.typography: Letterspaced uppercase caps for the toggle labels; serif headline over the hero

interactive_mechanics: Short slider flips hero photography between day and night lighting states
Single dominant control in the first viewport - nothing competes for the click
Scene re-lighting rather than overlay dimming
usability_notes: A masterclass in restraint: one metaphor, one control, placed where the decision lives. Works because the physical switch maps directly to the product's core value (light). Generalizes to any product with a day/night or before/after axis (real estate, lighting, hospitality). Travel should stay short and the label explicit; photography swap must be preloaded to avoid flash. Source: design-review writeup (dokle.design); live site not fetched.
